pr.title: Avoid some redundant work in GVN
pr.description:
The first 2 commits are about reducing the perf effect.

Third commit avoids doing redundant work: is a local is SSA, it already has been simplified, and the resulting value is in `self.locals`. No need to call any code on it.

The last commit avoids removing some storage statements.

r? wg-mir-opt
pr.author: cjgillot

processing.reason: The PR and its MIR-opt diffs only alter compiler-internal MIR shape: `rev_locals` becomes an IndexVec, `unsized_locals` is cached, SSA lhs values are read from `self.locals` instead of re-simplified, and self-place/self-index rewrites are no longer recorded so `StorageLive`/`StorageDead` are not replaced with `nop`. The issue_67019 diff merely removes a duplicate identical `ALLOC2`. These are redundant-work/perf and allocation-dedup changes with no semantic effect on defined Rust executions: retained vs removed storage markers and deduplicated equal constant allocations do not change any function's returned value. The frozen analysis itself states the observed differences are "MIR shape (storage statements and allocation duplication), not a demonstrated miscompile." Thus no ordinary-Rust pair with identical signatures/inputs can exhibit different original/transformed values grounded in this historical transformation; constructing one would require an arbitrary unrelated value change, which is disallowed.

analysis.summary: GVN perf PR (Camille Gillot, "Avoid some redundant work in GVN") makes four changes: rev_locals becomes an IndexVec, unsized_locals lookup is cached and SmallVec is used, SSA locals are no longer re-simplified because their value is already cached in self.locals, and self/self place rewrites are no longer recorded as replacements so StorageLive/StorageDead statements are not removed. Reusable knowledge: GVN must only remember a place rewrite when the replacement local actually differs; otherwise it marks the local as reused and erases storage statements. It should use the cached value for an SSA lhs instead of re-running simplify_rvalue.
analysis.originalLogic: In GVN's VnState::visit_statement, an assignment `lhs = rvalue` was simplified by calling `self.simplify_rvalue(rvalue, location)` (unless the rvalue is a constant), then trying `try_as_constant`/`try_as_local`. Separately, simplify_place_projection rewrote `place.local` to `try_as_local(base, location)` and an `Index(local)` projection to `try_as_local(idx, location)`, inserting the chosen local into `reused_locals` regardless of whether it differed from the existing local. The PR describes the old behavior as: "is a local is SSA, it already has been simplified, and the resulting value is in `self.locals`. No need to call any code on it." and "The last commit avoids removing some storage statements."
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically incorrect transformation stored self-replacements: `place.local = new_local` was recorded even when `place.local == new_local`, and `ProjectionElem::Index(idx_local)` was replaced by `Index(new_idx_local)` even when `idx_local == new_idx_local`. Because the pass inserted that same local into `reused_locals`, later handling treated the local as reused and replaced its storage statements with `nop` (test diffs show `StorageLive(_2);`/`StorageDead(_2);` being replaced by `nop`). It also re-simplified an SSA lhs even though `self.locals[local]` already held its simplified value, which could produce redundant work and duplicate constant allocations (issue_67019 diff removes a second `ALLOC2` containing the same `01 02` bytes). The corrected transformation is: use the cached value first with `lhs.as_local()`, `self.locals[local]`, and `.or_else(|| self.simplify_rvalue(rvalue, location))`; guard base rewrites with `&& place.local != new_local`; guard index rewrites with `idx_local != new_idx_local`; and return instead of falling through to super_statement for assignments.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR functions processed by rustc_mir_transform's GVN pass, especially functions with SSA locals, local assignments whose lhs is already in `self.locals`, place projections containing local bases and `ProjectionElem::Index`, mutable-reference/deref patterns, slice indexing, and constant-propagation results that GVN turns into constants. The relevant trigger is a MIR place whose `try_as_local` resolves back to the same local, or an assignment whose lhs local already has a cached VnIndex.
analysis.trigger: During GVN statement visiting, an assignment target is an SSA local whose value is already in `self.locals`, or `simplify_place_projection` calls `try_as_local` and receives the same local already present in the place (`place.local == new_local`) / the same index local (`idx_local == new_idx_local`). Under the old code this self-match was recorded in `reused_locals`, so the corresponding StorageLive/StorageDead were later replaced with `nop`; the old code also re-simplified the SSA lhs rvalue instead of using the cached value.
preconditions: The function is being processed by the GVN MIR pass (compiler/rustc_mir_transform/src/gvn.rs).
The place's base local or index local is SSA and `try_as_local` can resolve a dominating assignment for the same value.
`self.locals` already contains the simplified VnIndex for an SSA lhs local.
The local is otherwise eligible for storage-statement removal via `reused_locals`.
pitfalls: Do not treat a self-replacement (`new_local == place.local` or `new_idx_local == idx_local`) as a reuse; doing so unnecessarily removes StorageLive/StorageDead (they become `nop`).
Do not re-simplify an SSA lhs when `self.locals[local]` is already populated; this is redundant and can create duplicate constant allocations as seen in issue_67019.
Separate the two concerns: the cached-value shortcut for SSA lhs is one optimization, while guarding no-op place replacements is what preserves storage statements.
Borrowing/deref and post-copy overwrite restrictions are separate conditions; a same-local projection rewrite is not evidence of a validity bug by itself.
This is a performance/optimization PR, not a confirmed semantic bug fix; the observed differences are MIR shape (storage statements and allocation duplication), not a demonstrated miscompile.
analysis.testStrategy: Use MIR-opt tests that dump GVN output (`tests/mir-opt/gvn.*.GVN.*.diff`, `tests/mir-opt/const_prop/*.GVN.*.diff`, `tests/mir-opt/const_allocation*.GVN.after.*.mir`). Construct paired inputs differing only in the triggering condition: (a) a place where `try_as_local` resolves to the same local, versus (b) a place where it resolves to a distinct dominating local. In variant (a), verify StorageLive/StorageDead remain present and no duplicate ALLOC is emitted; in variant (b), verify legitimate reuse still replaces the place and may remove storage. Also compare an SSA lhs assignment (should read `self.locals` and avoid re-simplification) against a non-SSA lhs that must run simplify_rvalue. Check the issue_67019 and transmute.unreachable_mut diffs for duplicated allocation removal and preserved StorageLive/StorageDead. No compiler was built and no execution/reproduction is claimed.
evidence: Avoid some redundant work in GVN
Third commit avoids doing redundant work: is a local is SSA, it already has been simplified, and the resulting value is in `self.locals`. No need to call any code on it.
The last commit avoids removing some storage statements.
